summary: Olympic NF cupola lookout built 1917 in Clallam County, WA; 1996 replica torn down in October 2012 after vandalism; site kept as a viewpoint.

facts.design: D-6 wooden cupola groundhouse (original, 1917); the 1996 replica reproduced the cupola design
facts.status_note: The 1996 replica was torn down in October 2012 after vandalism.

events.note: Original D-6 cupola cabin. Wikipedia and a 2003 register visit note say 1920s.
Original cab destroyed. FFLOS gives 1962; firelookout.com gives 1963.
Replica built on the site. Wikipedia gives 1997.
Replica torn down in October 2012 after vandalism.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1917 matches the register and firelookout.com for the first D-6 cupola cab. The 1920s dates from Wikipedia and a 2003 register visit note are treated as looser estimates.
The register and the Former Fire Lookout Sites register both say 1996. Wikipedia says 1997. We follow the two 1996 sources.
The register credits the Forest Service with the 1996 rebuild, and firelookout.com names state, federal and private funding. The two accounts name different things and do not contradict each other.

notes_for_editor: No WebSearch was available in this run (the turn's shared search budget was used up before this lookout), so no newspaper or Forest Service article on the 2012 removal was read. The Forest Service newsroom page cited in the record (fs.usda.gov/detail/olympic, cid STELPRDB5395074) was read and is a generic newsroom with nothing on this lookout. Wikipedia cites a USDA Forest Service 'Kloshe Nanitch Observation Site' page that we did not locate. Unresolved: original destroyed 1962 (FFLOS) vs 1963 (firelookout.com); built 1917 vs 1920s; elevation 959 m (NHLR, used in our record) vs 927 m (FFLOS, 3,040 ft). The NHLR visit form shows 'Staffed? Yes' but its text gives no staffing dates, so staffing is not stated. The site's current state (viewpoint, road access) rests on Wikipedia alone. The NHLR visit notes predate the 2012 removal. Gone-site wording: the story says no source describes the remains.
